samples.text:
Since the pandemic, many companies allow their staff to work from home. Some people think this is better for employees, but others believe working in an office with colleagues is more effective. This essay will discuss both views and give my opinion.

There are many advantages of working from home. Firstly, employees do not need to travel to work every day, so they save time and money. For example, a person who spend two hours in traffic every day can use this time to sleep more or spend with his family. Secondly, people can organise their own schedule and work in a quiet place without interruption from colleagues. Many workers also say they feel less stress at home.

However, working in an office also has important benefits. When people work together in the same place, it is easier to communicate and solve problems quickly. New employees can learn from experienced colleagues by watching them and asking questions. In addition, some people feel lonely when they work at home alone for a long time, and they miss the chance to make friend at work. It can be also difficult to separate work and private life, because the office is in the living room.

In my opinion, the best solution is to mix both ways. Employees can work from home two or three days a week and go to the office on other days for meetings and teamwork. This give workers flexibility and also keep good communication in the company.

In conclusion, working from home and working in an office both have advantages. I believe that a combination of the two is the most effective way for employees and companies.
samples.why: Both views discussed with a clear opinion · relevant examples but limited development · mechanical linking (Firstly, Secondly, In addition) · adequate vocabulary · several agreement and word-order errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
Remote working has become far more common in recent years, and opinions differ on whether it is a positive development. Some people believe working from home benefits employees, while others argue that an office environment is more productive. In my view, both arrangements have clear strengths, and a flexible combination is the most effective option.

Supporters of home working highlight the improvement it brings to employees' quality of life. Without a daily commute, workers save considerable time and money, which they can spend on rest, exercise or family commitments. Many people also find they can concentrate better at home, away from the noise and constant interruptions of an open-plan office. Furthermore, remote work allows people to live further from expensive city centres, and it makes employment more accessible for parents and those with disabilities.

On the other hand, there are important advantages to working alongside colleagues. Face-to-face contact makes communication quicker and more natural, and informal conversations often lead to new ideas that would never come up in scheduled video calls. Office working is particularly valuable for younger employees, who learn a great deal simply by observing more experienced staff. In addition, some people struggle with isolation at home and find it difficult to switch off when their workplace is also their living space.

In my opinion, the question is not which option is better, but how to combine them effectively. A hybrid model, in which employees spend part of the week at home for focused tasks and come into the office for collaboration and training, offers most of the benefits of each approach while reducing their drawbacks.

In conclusion, although working from home offers greater freedom and comfort, the office remains important for teamwork and learning, and I believe a hybrid arrangement serve both employees and employers best.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · both views extended with relevant detail · logical organisation and varied linking · good collocations (daily commute, open-plan office) · frequent error-free sentences with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The widespread adoption of remote working has prompted a reassessment of where work is best done. Some believe that working from home is clearly preferable for employees, while others maintain that an office shared with colleagues is more effective. In my view, each setting suits different kinds of work, and the most productive arrangement is one that combines them deliberately.

The case for home working rests largely on autonomy and wellbeing. Eliminating the commute gives employees back hours each week and reduces both travel costs and stress. Many find that a quiet home environment enables sustained concentration that is difficult to achieve amid the distractions of a busy office. Remote work also widens access to employment, allowing people with caring responsibilities, health conditions or homes far from urban centres to participate more fully in the workforce.

Nevertheless, the office offers benefits that are not easily replicated online. Collaboration is often more fluid in person, where questions can be resolved in moments and chance conversations can spark ideas that would never surface in a scheduled video call. For those early in their careers, proximity to experienced colleagues is an invaluable, if informal, form of training. There is also a social dimension: prolonged remote working can leave people isolated, and the blurring of boundaries between home and work can make it hard to switch off.

Framing the issue as a choice between the two is therefore unhelpful. Tasks requiring deep concentration are often best carried out at home, whereas teamwork, mentoring and relationship-building benefit from shared physical space. Organisations should adopt hybrid arrangements designed around the nature of the work rather than habit, giving employees flexibility while preserving the collaborative culture that offices foster.

In conclusion, while working from home offers clear advantages for employees' comfort and focus, the office remains essential for collaboration and learning. A thoughtfully designed combination of the two is likely to serve both employees and organisations best.
samples.why: Both views fully developed with precise support · clear, well-reasoned position · skilful cohesion and paragraphing · wide, natural vocabulary (proximity, sustained concentration) · wide range of complex structures, error-free.
